name: Jubal
overview: Jubal is a male figure in the early biblical narrative, recognized as the father of all who play the lyre and pipe. His identity is primarily defined by this unique attribute, highlighting his foundational role in the development of musical arts according to Genesis 4:21. There is no additional tribal affiliation or extensive notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Jubal appears as a proper name in Genesis 4:21. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is provided, so it is simply acknowledged as his given name in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Jubal as a son of Lamech and Adah, indicating his place within a particular family lineage. These relationships are inferred from the same verse that mentions his unique contribution to music.
scriptureSignificance: Jubal's significance lies in his designation as the originator of musical instruments such as the lyre and pipe, marking him as a pioneering figure in the cultural and artistic development of humanity. His mention in Genesis situates him within the early generations after Adam, emphasizing the God-ordained progress of human creativity. This highlights the biblical theme that God has endowed mankind with talents and roles that contribute to civilization.
